item.title: Feds launch fair housing probe into North Texas development marketed to Muslims
item.description: AUSTIN (Texas Tribune) -- The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development is investigating whether two development companies behind a master-planned North Texas community formerly known as East Plano Islamic Center City discriminated against people’s religion or national origin. The investigation comes after several state officials accused entities behind the development that marketed to Muslims [...]

item.title: Texas 10-runs UC Davis in season opener
item.description: Mendoza smacked a towering drive over the left field wall near the visitor's bullpen, plating Anthony Pack Jr. and Temo Becerra to turn a 9-2 lead into a mercy-rule victory.

item.title: Texas A&M student Brianna Aguilera's death was suicide, medical examiner's report says
item.description: A Texas A&M student who fell off a West Campus high rise in Austin on Nov. 29, 2025 had died by suicide, according to a report released Friday by the Travis County Medical Examiner's Office.

item.title: Texas-UC Davis baseball moved up Saturday due to forecasted storms
item.description: The teams kicked off the college baseball season with the opener Friday night, and the game Sunday is slated to start at noon, unaffected by weather.

item.title: AG Paxton seeks information for BCBS; Conduent data breach
item.description: Attor­ney Gen­er­al Ken Pax­ton is demanding information from Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas (BCBS) and Con­duent Business Services, LLC (Conduent) as part of an inves­ti­ga­tion into "largest data breach in U.S. history," according to a news release from Paxton's office.

item.title: Showers and storms on Saturday, low severe risk
item.description: Valentine's Day plans are soggy, with showers and thunderstorms expected tomorrow in Central Texas. -- Meteorologist Tommy House

item.title: Texas Attorney General says state suing cord blood banking company
item.description: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton announced in a Friday morning press release that he had sued CBR Systems, a CooperSurgical subsidiary that provides cord blood storage, for allegedly deceptive trade practices.

item.title: Friendship, inclusivity take center stage at Special Olympics Texas Winter Games, Leadership Conference
item.description: As Olympic competition heats up in Italy, more than a thousand athletes from across the state arrived in Central Texas for the 2026 Special Olympics Texas Winter Games.

item.title: Hutto ISD's apprenticeship program grows as teacher vacancies falls
item.description: Two years after Hutto ISD launched its teacher apprenticeship program, district leaders say it has helped create the district’s own teacher pipeline.

item.title: Student-led anti-ICE walkouts continue on Central Texas campuses amid state pressure
item.description: Students at multiple schools in Texas are walking out in protest of increased immigration enforcement, including at campuses in Round Rock Independent School District and Austin Independent School District.
